content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text treats a chain-vs-chain collision (descent according to the flesh against conception of the Holy Ghost) as underdetermined because there is no explicit textual resolution of paternity, which is the kind of stating-verse requirement K-C addresses.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "never verse by verse / that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires: (1) explicit textual resolution is not required; the chains must be weighed by footing, or (2) absence of an explicit resolving verse makes the matter underdetermined; the judge used (2).", "why": "The judge labels the link underdetermined for lacking explicit textual resolution of paternity, which is the retired stating-verse approach rather than a chain-by-footing assessment required by K-C."}
